summary: James Wilkinson Breeks (1830–1872) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (~1849–1851) and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1852 to 1872.

James Wilson (1853–1926) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1870–1874) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1874–1875), and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1873 to 1910.

James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist who earned his undergraduate degree at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and his PhD at Johns Hopkins (~1879–1882). He taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins (1905–1925).

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (1846–1912) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. He studied under teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught numerous students, including Shenphen Nangwa and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

The 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge (1954–1992) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Tekchok Dorje, and taught students including Karma Tashi Chophel, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University, under Kazuo Okabe, and under Minoru Kiyota at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD), later holding professorships in Buddhist, East Asian, and religious studies at Smith College.
Jampa Lhundup works in Tibetology and linguistics. As of 2026, he is attested as having studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, where he also served on the faculty.

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning a Geshe Lharampa at Sera Monastery and studying at the University of Munich, he held editorial and research posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1974–2005).
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Jampa Samten works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Attested as a bibliographer at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 1987, he later served as Director (2003–2004) and Professor (2015, 2026) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jampal Kunzang Rechung (born 1930) is a Tibetology scholar. He served as Deputy Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1982) and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1980–1988).

Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (1912–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Kalu Rinpoche, Chatral Sangye Dorje, and the 13th Dalai Lama, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama and the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsab, and others. He succeeded Dzongsar Khyentse Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo and taught figures including Namkhai Norbu, Dilgo Khyentse, and Sogyal Rinpoche.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies master. He studied under teachers including Rigdzin Zangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Jan A. Schoterman (1948–1989) was an Indologist. He earned his degrees, including a PhD under Henk Bodewitz and Jan Gonda, at Utrecht University, and held posts at Utrecht, Tilburg University, and the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies.

Jan Brunson works in Indology. She completed a PhD at Brown University (-2008), served as Visiting Assistant Professor at Bowdoin College (2008–2011), and was Affiliate Faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 2011.

Jan C. Heesterman (1925–2014) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate under Jan Gonda (~1953–1957). He served as a professor at Leiden University from 1964 to 1990, succeeding F. B. J. Kuiper in 1972.

Jan Chozen Bays (born 1945) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Swarthmore College and UC San Diego, she trained under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada, taught with the Zen Community of Oregon, and became abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery.
